summary: A 1970 note on the aftermath of a network meeting, with an epilogue and miscellaneous items. It records outcomes and follow-up points rather than defining a protocol.

eli5.summary: This is a follow-up after a meeting, like the notes you send out afterward to remind everyone what happened.

questions: what was discussed at the march 1970 network meeting
what is a process in networking
why are sockets important in early network protocol
subtitle: Notes from an early network protocol design meeting in 1970

tldr.problem: Early ARPANET developers needed to coordinate on protocol design and share feedback after meetings.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 37 documents a March 1970 network meeting discussing protocol modifications including dynamic reconnection, and records follow-up conversations.
tldr.outcome: This artifact captures the early design discussions that shaped network protocol development, including debates about sockets, connections, and links.

today: RFC 37 is a historical record of early ARPANET protocol discussions and has not been obsoleted. It documents the evolution of socket-based network communications that became foundational to Internet protocols.

sections.title: Meeting Record
sections.content: On March 17, 1970, Steve Crocker hosted a network meeting at UCLA with about 25 people from sites across the ARPANET, including MIT, BBN, Harvard, SRI, Utah, UCSB, and others. The meeting discussed modifications to the host protocol based on work documented in earlier RFCs, with a focus on adding dynamic reconnection capabilities.
sections.eli5: Computer scientists from different places met to discuss how to make the network protocol better and more flexible.

sections.title: The Protocol Debate
sections.content:
The main topic was moving from a login-based protocol to one based on sockets and simplex connections, as documented in RFC 33 and RFC 36. The new protocol made it possible to connect any two processes without requiring login. The group broadly accepted the approach, though some questioned the complexity, particularly around dynamic reconnection.

After the meeting, Crocker received follow-up suggestions from other sites, including ideas from Bill Crowther at BBN about alternative approaches to reconnection and whether connections and links should be decoupled. These discussions would influence ongoing protocol design.
sections.eli5: They argued about how computers should reconnect to each other: should connections and the actual communication links be separate ideas, or tied together?

sections.title: Defining Process
sections.content: RFC 37 formally defines what a process means in the network context: a program with an assigned location counter and address space, distinct from a passive program stored in a file. A process is created by an existing process and can terminate itself or be terminated by another process. This definition clarifies that sockets serve as a standard interface between processes, because processes cannot directly request connection with each other in a well-defined way.
sections.eli5: A 'process' is a running program with its own memory and identity. Sockets are like mailboxes that let different processes send messages to each other.
